question.text: The graph above shows the function $y=\tan{(Bx)}+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B+D?$
question.explanation:
The period $T$ of the function is

\[ T = \dfrac{3\pi}{2} - \left(-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{6\pi}{2}={3\pi} . \]

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\tan(Bx + C) + D$ is given by

\[ T = \dfrac{\pi}{B}. \]

Applying the formula of the period, we get

\[ {3\pi} = \dfrac{\pi}{B}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad B = \dfrac{\pi}{\left({3\pi}\right)} =\dfrac{1}{3} . \]

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the tangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $2$ units down. Hence, $D=-2.$

Therefore, $B+D= \left(\dfrac 1 3\right) + (-2)=-\dfrac{5}{3}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

\[ y=\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)-2 . \]

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y=\tan{(Bx)}+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B+D?$
question.explanation:
The period $T$ of the function is

\[ T = \dfrac{\pi}2 - \left( -\dfrac{\pi}2 \right) = \pi . \]

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\tan(Bx + C) + D$ is given by

\[ T = \dfrac{\pi}{B}. \]

Applying the formula of the period, we get

\[ \pi = \dfrac{\pi}{B}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad B = \dfrac{\pi}{\pi} = 1 . \]

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the tangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $2$ unit up. Hence, $D=2.$

Therefore, $B+D = 1+2 =3.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

\[ y=\tan\left({x}\right)+2 . \]

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y=\cot{(Bx)}+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B-D?$
question.explanation:
The period $T$ of the function is

\[ T = \dfrac{4\pi}{5} . \]

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\cot(Bx + C) + D$ is given by

\[ T = \dfrac{\pi}{B}. \]

Applying the formula of the period, we get

\[ \dfrac{4\pi}{5}= \dfrac{\pi}{B}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad B = \dfrac{\pi}{\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{5}\right)} = \dfrac54 . \]

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the cotangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $\dfrac{9}{4}$ units up. Hence, $D=\dfrac{9}{4}.$

Therefore, $B-D= \dfrac 54- \dfrac 94 =-1.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

\[ y=\cot\left(\dfrac{5x}4\right)+\dfrac{9}{4} . \]

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y = \cot(Bx) + D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B + D?$
question.explanation:
The period $T$ of the function is \[ T = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}-0 = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}. \]

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y = A\cot(Bx + C) + D$ is given by \[ T = \dfrac{\pi}{B}. \]

Applying the formula of the period, we get \[ \dfrac{4\pi}{3}= \dfrac{\pi}{B} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad B = \dfrac{\pi}{\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)} = \dfrac{3}{4}. \]

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the cotangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $3$ units down. Hence, $D = -3.$

Therefore, $B + D = \dfrac{3}{4} + (-3) = -\dfrac{9}{4}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is \[ y = \cot\left( \dfrac{3x}{4}\right) - 3. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Horizontal Shift of a Horizontally Stretched Tangent or Cotangent Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y=\tan{\left(\dfrac{x}{2}+C\right)},$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\dfrac{\pi}{2} < C < \dfrac{\pi}{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
question.explanation:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

\begin{align*} y & =\tan{\left( \dfrac x 2+C\right)}\\[5pt] & =\tan{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x+2C\right)\right)}\\[5pt] \end{align*}

The factor $x+2C$ indicates that the graph of $y=\tan{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x+2C\right)\right)}$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\tan\!\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$ by $\dfrac {\pi}{4}$ units to the left. Therefore:

\[ 2C= \dfrac{\pi}{4} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad C = \dfrac {\pi} {8} \]

example.title: Identifying the Horizontal Shift of a Horizontally Stretched Tangent or Cotangent Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y = \tan\left(2x + C\right),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\dfrac{\pi}{2} < C < \dfrac{\pi}{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
question.explanation:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows: \begin{align*} y & =\tan\left( 2x + C\right)\\[5pt] & = \tan\left(2\left(x + \dfrac{C}{2}\right) \right) \end{align*}

The factor $x+\dfrac{C}{2}$ indicates that the graph of $y=\tan\left(2\left(x+\dfrac{C}{2}\right)\right)$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\tan\left(2x\right).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\tan\left(2x\right)$ by $\dfrac{\pi}{12}$ units to the left. Therefore \[ \dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{12} \quad \Longrightarrow\quad C = \dfrac{\pi}{6}. \]

example.title: Identifying the Horizontal Shift of a Horizontally Stretched Tangent or Cotangent Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y=\cot{\left(\dfrac{2x}{3}+C\right)},$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\dfrac{\pi}{2} < C < \dfrac{\pi}{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
question.explanation:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

\begin{align*} y & =\cot{\left( \dfrac {2x} 3+C\right)}\\[5pt] & =\cot{\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\left(x+\dfrac{3C}{2}\right)\right)}\\[5pt] \end{align*}

The factor $x+\dfrac{3C}{2}$ indicates that the graph of $y=\cot\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\left(x+\dfrac{3C}{2}\right)\right)$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\cot\left(\dfrac{2x}{3}\right).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\cot\left(\dfrac{2x}{3}\right)$ by $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}-\dfrac{\pi}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ units to the left. Therefore:

\[ \dfrac{3C}{2}= \dfrac{\pi}{4} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad C = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad C =\dfrac{\pi}{6} \]

Since $-\dfrac{\pi}{2} < C < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{6}.$
